answer: For a poll on whether a sable trail should wander past a timber bridge, each ballot posts a $10 bond. A challenger may submit evidence that two ballots represent the same voter. A judge reviews it; if persuaded, the judge rejects both ballots and awards both bonds to the challenger. Otherwise the ballots count and bonds are refunded. Each ballot ties up $10; duplicates may go unchallenged, and judges can err.
